complexity.notes: The deque and Optional/List imports are assumed from the surrounding environment; as pasted, the snippet references them without importing. The traversal does more work than needed since it stores every node of every level only to keep the last one — a single pass that visits ||the right child before the left and records the first node seen at each depth|| would avoid building the full level lists, though it stays O(n) time. ||A BFS that keeps only the last dequeued node per level|| similarly trims the extra level storage.
complexity.summary: Runs a standard BFS level-order traversal, materializing each level as a list, then takes the last element of every level as the right-side view.
